Did you know Finnair Avios redemptions come with free connections in Northern Europe?

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:56
Instaread

Links on Head for Points may support the site by paying a commission.  See here for all partner links.

A press release from Finnair yesterday reminded me of a lesser-known feature of Avios redemptions on Finnair: free connections in Northern Europe.

Basically, you can add an extra flight to a Finnair Avios ticket for no extra cost to/from certain cities. This applies whether you book your Finnair flights via ba.com or transfer Avios across to Finnair Plus.

(You would, by the way, be shocked by how rarely an airline ever sends out a press release about its loyalty programme. IAG Loyalty, as a separate business, has its own team, but from other airlines it is usually tumbleweed.)

Here is the relevant wording from the website:

“When your award booking includes a connecting flight, Avios will be charged separately for each flight, except for flights within zone 1 (Finland and Northern Europe*).

Example: When you book a London–Helsinki–Singapore award flight, Avios are charged separately for the London–Helsinki flight and the Helsinki–Singapore flight. But when you book a Stockholm–Helsinki–Singapore award flight, we charge Avios only for the Helsinki–Singapore flight.”

The full list of eligible routes is:

  • Bodø (Norway)
  • Copenhagen (Denmark)
  • Gdansk (Poland)
  • Gothenburg (Sweden)
  • Ivalo (Finland)
  • Kirkenes (Norway)
  • Kittilä (Finland)
  • Kuusamo (Finland)
  • Oslo (Norway)
  • Riga (Latvia)
  • Rovaniemi (Finland – winter only)
  • Stockholm (Sweden)
  • Tallinn (Estonia)
  • Trondheim (Norway)
  • Umeå (Sweden)
  • Vilnius (Lithuania)
  • Visby (Sweden)
  • Warsaw (Poland)

Why this might be useful for you

What’s great about this is that it makes one-stop flights good value, which is rare with Avios.

If you fly on British Airways from Manchester to Lyon via Heathrow, for example, you are charged the cost of Manchester to Heathrow and Heathrow to Lyon added together. It’s a terrible deal for Avios – and of course, given the hassle of connecting at Heathrow, a terrible deal in terms of experience and flying time!

On Finnair, however, the cost of flying from Manchester to Rovaniemi via Helsinki is the same as flying from Manchester to Helsinki. The second flight is effectively free, which makes these trips great value for your Avios.

(Unfortunately, you can’t take advantage of this by having a free stopover in Helsinki. You must fly all the way through. You ARE allowed one stopover if you book a long-haul return Finnair redemption.)

There’s another reason you might find this useful.

Imagine that you want to fly to Osaka in Japan with Finnair.

You could fly from the UK to Helsinki to Osaka. To save Air Passenger Duty (£261 in business class from next April) you may decide to fly to Helsinki on a separate ticket.

Helsinki isn’t that easy to reach, however. Finnair flies from Heathrow, Manchester and Edinburgh but a lot of the UK is not covered. Since the Avios cost of, say, Stockholm to Helsinki to Osaka is the same as Helsinki to Osaka, you might find it easier to travel to Sweden on a budget carrier from your local airport and start from there.

How to book Finnair’s free Avios connections

Booking these flights is easy and can be done on finnair.com (the instructions for moving Avios to Finnair Plus are in this article) or ba.com.

Here’s an example from Finnair Plus to show it works. Here is Heathrow to Helsinki in economy:

.... and here is Heathrow to Rovaniemi, connecting in Helsinki:

It’s the same price at just 12,000 Avios each way, which is great value for what is almost a 5-hour trip with the connection. The only difference is an extra £6 in taxes.

PS. If you want to fly in business class, book on ba.com. Because the domestic flight is economy-only, it messes up the BA pricing algorithm! You’d pay 16,250 Avios + £75.45 to Rovaniemi (flying in business class from Heathrow to Helsinki) even though Finnair Plus wants 18,000 Avios and ba.com wants 18,000 Avios for just Heathrow to Helsinki!
